heading: EXT. DRIVE-IN SCREEN TOWER - ROOFTOP - NIGHT

units.text: EXT. DRIVE-IN SCREEN TOWER - ROOFTOP - NIGHT
The back of an enormous white screen, scaffolded and creaking, rises above a field of parked cars.
Light from the projection booth spills over the lot like milk.
Beyond the fence, cornfields roll dark to the horizon, silent as sea.
On a ladder platform two stories up, PERPETUA "PEPPER" LINDQVIST, 15, sits with her knees pulled to her chin.
Her denim jacket is covered in hand-sewn patches, each one a different band.
A bag of stolen popcorn sits beside her, untouched.
The wind ruffles her short hair.
She is watching the lot below as if memorizing it.
Far down the lot, a car door slams.
Laughter, faint.
Somebody's radio drifts: a slow song.
A boot rings on the scaffold below.
Pepper doesn't turn.
MILO ABARA, 16, climbs into view, lanky, glasses held to his face with tape at one hinge.
He carries a thermos like a trophy.
He sees her.
Stops.
I thought nobody came up here.
units.name: MILO

units.text: Nobody does.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: Then why are you up here?
units.name: MILO

units.text: Why are you?
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: He climbs the last rungs and sits, careful, at the far end of the platform, with the thermos between them like a border.
I work the snack bar. Third night. They don't pay me enough to be nice to people, so on my break I climb.
units.name: MILO

units.text: How'd you find it?
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: Fell off the ladder. Landed on the platform. Saw the view. Fell in love a little.
units.name: MILO

units.text: With the view.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: With being too high to hear anyone ask for extra butter.
units.name: MILO

units.text: She almost smiles.
Doesn't.
He unscrews the thermos, pours something steaming into the cap, and holds it out.
Hot chocolate. It's bad.
units.name: MILO

units.text: Bad how?
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: Powdered. Lumpy. But hot.
units.name: MILO

units.text: She takes it.
Drinks.
Makes a face.
Drinks again.
It's terrible.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: Told you.
units.name: MILO

units.text: My brother used to make it like this. Used to burn it on purpose because he said the burnt part was the good part.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: Where is he?
units.name: MILO

units.text: Army. Fort something. He sends postcards with no words. Just stamps.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: Stamps?
units.name: MILO

units.text: He picks the weirdest ones. Last time it was a stamp of a moth. I think it means he's okay.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: Or he misses you.
units.name: MILO

units.text: Or the post office only had moths.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: Milo laughs, too loud.
The sound carries.
She shushes him, laughing herself, and they both look down.
Below, a flashlight beam sweeps the fence line, bored, unhurried.
They both freeze, shoulders touching.
Pepper puts a finger to her lips.
Milo nods, eyes huge behind his taped glasses.
The beam passes.
Slides along the scaffold.
Pauses at the platform edge.
Passes on.
They breathe again.
That's twice you've almost gotten me arrested.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: It's the first time we've met.
units.name: MILO

units.text: You know what I mean.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: I really don't.
units.name: MILO

units.text: Fine. Next time, bring better chocolate.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: There's going to be a next time?
units.name: MILO

units.text: You tell me. You work here.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: Milo goes red to the ears.
He fumbles with the thermos cap.
Drops it.
They both lunge for it and knock heads.
Both freeze, rubbing their foreheads, and then both start laughing, silent shaking laughter, hands clamped over their mouths.
Down in the lot, the movie's climactic music swells.
A kiss, perhaps, on the big white screen they can't see from behind.
A car horn honks, a cheer, a ripple of applause.
Pepper wipes her eyes.
The laughter has turned into something else, quieter.
She looks at the dark cornfields.
My mom's selling the house in June.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: Where are you going?
units.name: MILO

units.text: Don't know yet. Somewhere with a lot of stamps, I guess.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: You could stay.
units.name: MILO

units.text: With who?
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: Milo looks at his sneakers.
At his hands.
At the thermos cap in them.
I don't know. Me, maybe. Eventually.
units.name: MILO

units.text: You're sixteen.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: Sixteen and a half.
units.name: MILO

units.text: That's not a plan, Milo.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: It's the start of one.
units.name: MILO

units.text: She looks at him for a long moment.
In the light from the booth, her face is open, young, unguarded.
Okay. A start.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: She takes the thermos cap from his hand, pours a last splash of terrible chocolate, and clinks it against his.
To moths.
units.name: PEPPER

units.text: To moths.
units.name: MILO

units.text: They drink.
The song on the radio ends.
Another begins.
